Please note that there are additional showtimes of 14TH that screen without open captions (on-screen display of dialogue and sounds). For those showtimes, click here.

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Animated Shorts
movies.description: These meticulously animated works of art follow a wide range of fascinating characters, from an Olympic swimmer who survived the Holocaust to an intrepid kid bravely attempting to rescue her village. Please note that some films contain disturbing material and may not be suitable for very young children. Butterfly Dir. Florence Miailhe France, 15min A poignant retelling of Olympic swimmer Alfred Nakache’s life, from his rise to fame to surviving Auschwitz, presented as memories flashing back during his final swim. Forevergreen Dirs. Nathan Engelhardt & Jeremy Spears US, 13min A joyful adventure featuring an orphaned bear cub and a fatherly tree turns serious when the cub is tempted by the allure of easy food. Fire and deadly danger ensue as the cub is left bereft of hope and on the verge of a ruinous end, until the sacrificial love of the tree falls into place. The Girl Who Cried Pearls Dirs. Chris Lavis & Maciek Szczerbowski Canada, 17min A haunting fable about a girl overwhelmed by sorrow, the boy who loves her, and how greed leads good hearts to wicked deeds. Retirement Plan Dir. John Kelly Ireland, 7min Ray (voiced by Domhall Gleeson) fantasizes about everything he’d love to do in retirement, once he finally has the “time.” The Three Sisters Dir. Konstantin Bronzit Israel & Cyprus, 14min Three sisters live a lonely life on an isolated island, each in their own small house. One day, circumstances change, and they are forced to rent out one of the houses. Also screening in this program: Éiru Dir. Giovanna Ferrari Ireland, 13min When the water mysteriously disappears from the well in a warrior clan’s village, an intrepid child descends into the belly of the earth to retrieve it. Éiru is the story of a kid in search of a challenge and a goddess in search of a champion.

movies.title: 2026 Oscar Nominated Live-Action Shorts
movies.description: These Oscar-contending films from Israel, the UK, the US, and France explore the messy, beautiful, and often forbidden ways we seek connection. Butcher’s Stain Dir. Meyer Levinson-Blount Israel, 26min Samir, a Palestinian butcher working at an Israeli supermarket, is accused of tearing down the Israeli hostage posters in the break room. Samir sets out to prove his innocence in order to keep the job he so desperately needs. A Friend of Dorothy Dir. Lee Knight UK, 21min Dorothy is a lonely widow whose body is failing but whose mind remains sharp as ever. When 17-year-old JJ accidentally kicks his football into her garden, an unlikely friendship blossoms. Jane Austen’s Period Drama Dirs. Steve Pinder & Julia Aks US, 12min In 1813 England, Essy Talbot’s long-awaited marriage proposal takes a messy turn when her period arrives at a very bad time. The Singers Dir. Sam A. Davis US, 18min The Singers is a film adaptation of a 19th-century short story written by Ivan Turgenev, in which downtrodden patrons in a lowly pub connect unexpectedly through an impromptu sing-off. Two People Exchanging Saliva Dirs. Natalie Musteata & Alexandre Singh France, 36min In a society where kissing is punishable by death and people pay for things by receiving slaps to the face, an unhappy woman shops compulsively in a department store and becomes entranced by one of the employees.

movies.title: 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple
movies.cast: Ralph Fiennes, Alfie Williams, Jack O'Connell, Erin Kellyman, Chi Lewis-Parry, Connor Newall
movies.description: The nature of the infected is changing… Director Nia DaCosta expands the grisly, post-apocalyptic world first forged by Danny Boyle and Alex Garland with 2002’s 28 Days Later and built upon in 2025’s 28 Years Later . In this third entry, Dr. Kelson (Fiennes) forms a relationship whose consequences could alter the fate of humanity, while Spike’s (Williams) encounter with Jimmy Crystal (O’Connell) spirals into a nightmare he can’t escape. In the world of The Bone Temple, the infected are no longer the greatest threat to survival—the inhumanity of the survivors proves far more terrifying.

movies.title: 7 Women
movies.cast: Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, Margaret Leighton, Flora Robson, Mildred Dunnock, Betty Field
movies.description: For his final film, the preeminent poet of the American West on screen lit out for the East, or at least a soundstage version of it—and eschewed his usual masculine ensembles for a decidedly more feminine group. Ford’s swansong takes place among a group of female Christian missionaries—Anne Bancroft, Sue Lyon, and Margaret Leighton among their number—in a c. 1935 rural China ravaged by cholera and ransacked by Mongolian warlord Tunga Khan (hulking wrestler Mike Mazurki), whose horde, including Ford regular Woody Strode, pose a clear and present danger to the ladies’ redoubt. “Ford brings a mix of rigor and playfulness, of something hieratic and something erratic, because he allows a bit of playfulness into the game and puts himself into it… The truth, in Ford’s films, is not at the end of the trail, but always before there has even been a road.” —Serge Daney

movies.title: A Clockwork Orange
movies.cast: Malcolm McDowell, Patrick Magee, Carl Duering, Michael Bates, Warren Clarke, James Marcus
movies.description: Wendy Carlos’s score of switched-on Moog synthesizer classical, Kubrick’s punchy framings, and Malcolm McDowell’s cruelly charismatic, Nadsat slang-spouting performance as teen reprobate Alex combine to make for cracking cinema, and a hallucinatory imagination of a future broken Britain. Based on the stinging satire by Anthony Burgess, a work by turns exhilarating and nauseating, the film of A Clockwork Orange would be withdrawn from British cinemas at Kubrick’s behest, citing concern over reports that it had inspired copycat crimes in the UK.

movies.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon
movies.cast: Soraya Akhlaghi
movies.country: France, UK, USA, Denmark, Iran, Austria
movies.description:
Pre-recorded Q&A with filmmakers Soraya Akhlaghi & Mehrdad Oskouei, moderated by DOC NYC’s Jaie Laplante, Thu, Dec 3 at 7:00 show!

Sixteen-year-old Soraya is a strong-willed Afghan sculptor and illustrator trying to find a way out of Iran and join her mother in Austria. This subtly textured self-portrait, shot by Soraya with her cell phone camera and directed by Mehrdad Oskouei, interweaves Soraya’s illustrations with chilling scenes of her escape attempts, political news from Afghanistan, and videos in which she sings and dances, or shows the bruises inflicted by her violent husband. Through masterful cinematography often filmed in dangerous conditions – and the protagonist’s radiant energy – this empowering collaboration between an established filmmaker and a young new artist enables her to reclaim her identity. Winner: Best Film, International Competition – IDFA 2025

“Inventive and engaging. A compelling, shape-shifting blend of thriller and dark fairy tale.” – Screen Daily

movies.title: A Separation
movies.cast: Payman Maadi, Leila Hatami, Shahab Hosseini, Sareh Bayat, Sarina Farhadi, Ali-Asghar Shahbazi
movies.description: Farhadi combines elements of the domestic drama and psychological thriller in his trenchant, lacerating 2012 Academy Award winner for Best Foreign Film. Simin (Leila Hatami) wants to emigrate with her 11-year-old daughter and with or without her husband, Nader (Payman Maadi), who, with the support of the court, has dug in his heels to keep the family in place while he looks after his ailing father, aided by a caregiver with costly secrets. Through the intersecting stories of two deadlocked couples—one middle-class, the other working-class—and their necessary deceptions, Farhadi shows us a microcosm of contemporary Iranian society and the insoluble moral dilemmas it presents to ordinary men and women.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: A Tale of the Wind
movies.cast: Joris Ivens, Liu Zhuang, Wang Delong, Wang Hong, Fu Dalin, Liu Guilian
movies.description: Almost 60 years after the completion of his first film, Netherlands-born Ivens arrived in China, where he’d first traveled in 1938—here the Gobi Desert, the Dazu Rock Carvings, the Terracotta Army, and the Leshan Giant Buddha all receive visits—to produce this elliptical, ruminative last will and testament comprised of “dreams, dramatized myths and real life” [The New York Times], effortlessly reconciling cinema’s documentary and fantasy traditions. The story of a life spent, in Ivens’s words, trying to “tame the wind and harness the sea,” and a strikingly calm goodbye from a filmmaker who spent so much time focusing on the seemingly ceaseless upheavals of the 20th century.

movies.title: Afternoons of Solitude
movies.cast: Andrés Roca Rey, Roberto Domínguez, Francisco Manuel "Viruta" Durán, Antonio Chacón, Paco Gómez, Manuel "Larita" Lara
movies.description: Serra’s visceral yet elegant documentary portrait of young, Peruvian-born superstar torero Andrés Roca Rey sees him risking life and limb on the clock, and in unglamorous off-hours traveling via minibus between arenas with an extensive, officious entourage. A privileged, patiently observed perspective on the flamboyant showmanship, ritualized grace, and terrible violence of bullfighting, that most controversial of the sporting arts, its time-honored spectacle of man’s cultivated, calculated intelligence facing down an elemental force of primal animal aggression, a spectacle that ends, invariably, in a welter of hot, bubbling blood. “Impressionistic and intimate… Perhaps the most immersive encapsulation of tauromachy yet achieved in cinema.” —Sight & Sound

movies.title: All of a Sudden
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Tao Okamoto, Kyōzō Nagatsuka, Kodai Kurosaki, Jean-Charles Clichet, Marie Bunel
movies.description: In the latest film by Oscar®-winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi (DRIVE MY CAR), Virginie Efira (BENEDETTA) stars as Marie-Lou, the progressive director of a nursing home in the Parisian suburbs. Her life changes when she meets Mari (Tao Okamoto), Japanese playwright. As the two women reckon with the lives they have lived, they find new ways to make sense of the time that remains. Following caregivers as they navigate the tensions between idealism and pragmatism, Hamaguchi crafts a film that rests fully in the present, attentive to the delicate unfolding of thought, feeling, and human connection.

movies.title: All the Long Nights
movies.cast: Hokuto Matsumura, Mone Kamishiraishi, Kiyohiko Shibukawa, Sawako Fujima, Haruka Imou, Maki Kubota
movies.description: Based on the novel of the same name by Maiko Seo, Miyake’s tender, understated drama stars Hokuto Matsumura and Mone Kamishiraishi as two co-workers who, after discovering they both suffer from invisibly debilitating conditions little understood by the wider world—he from blindsiding panic attacks, she from wild PMS-related mood swings—form a tentative bond based on mutual respect and care. Often affecting but never given to unearned sentiment, abhorrent of cliché, caricature, and easy scapegoating, All The Long Nights is a deeply humane film about the everyday hurdles faced in muddling through life, buoyed by the considerable chemistry of its irresistible leads.

movies.title: Alpha
movies.cast: Mélissa Boros, Tahar Rahim, Golshifteh Farahani, Emma Mackey, Finnegan Oldfield, Louai El Amrousy
movies.description: Life swiftly starts to unravel for Alpha and her single mom after the rebellious 13-year-old comes home with a stick-and-poke tattoo made with a used needle at a house party—a mark that may be related to a contagious blood-borne disease that turns its victims into disintegrating stone. The third feature by French director and screenwriter Julia Ducournau, winner of the Palme d’Or at the 2021 Cannes Film Festival for Titane , is a mysterious, unsettling allegory for the 1980s AIDS crisis and the waves of hysteria, prejudice, and exclusion it produced.

movies.title: American Boucaniste
movies.description:
American Boucaniste (dir. Javier Merizalde, 2026)

For more than 20 years, Charlie Mysak’s bookstand occupied the corner of Columbus Ave. and 68th St. in Manhattan’s Upper West Side, selling books, records and other paraphernalia to famous and regular pedestrians alike, even getting into trouble with the law. This is the story of one of the last street book vendors in New York City.
notes: Tickets: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/american-boucaniste-tickets-2005487856164?aff=oddtdtcreator

movies.title: An Autumn Afternoon
movies.cast: Chishū Ryū, Shima Iwashita, Keiji Sada, Mariko Okada, Teruo Yoshida, Noriko Maki
movies.description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping consumerism has become more bitter here, the feeling of incoming winter chill is sharper, the entire project imbued with a tang of regret—incidentally, the title literally translates to “The Taste of Autumn Mackerel.”

movies.title: An Evening With The New York Times Op-Docs 2026, Part 2
movies.director: Amélie Hardy, Joshua Oppenheimer, Lotte Salomons, Pawel Chorzepa, Taliesin Black-Brown
movies.description:
A WOLF IN THE SUBURBS (Amélie Hardy) — Welcome to Mississauga, Ontario, where lawns are clipped, neighbors are watchful and no blade of grass dares misbehave. Except at Wolf Ruck’s place. His lawn grows wild, and so does the trouble.

THE REVOLUTION AGAINST DEATH (Joshua Oppenheimer) — A faded rococo resort hosts a revolution against aging and death. Amid turquoise pools, gilt and chintz, fear is in the air — of illness, of invisibility, of having no one to hold or hear us, of dying alone. A film poem about mortality, fear, the longing to remain when you know you can’t.

SANYI KAKAS (SANYI THE ROOSTER) (Lotte Salomons) — In 2020, a rooster escapes in Békéscsaba, Hungary. For four years, the locals care for him as a beloved symbol of hope and unity — until his sudden, mysterious death replaces harmony with suspicion and division.

THE TUNERS (Pawel Chorzepa) — In the shadows of the International Chopin Piano Competition, the world’s most important piano contest, expert tuners spend a month trying to achieve the perfect pitch.

LISTEN (Taliesin Black-Brown) — As his mother slips away into dementia, an Alaskan sound recordist listens for what remains.
notes: Join us for a special presentation of five acclaimed short documentaries from The New York Times Op-Docs, followed by a discussion with the filmmakers. This program features:
Wed Dec 2: Q&A w/ filmmakers at 6:30!

movies.title: And Your Bird Can Sing preceded by August 8th
movies.description:
“Among Sho Miyake's most quietly luminous works, And Your Bird Can Sing is a tender and deeply felt portrait of youth poised between freedom and uncertainty. Adapted from Yasushi Sato's novel and set in the port city of Hakodate, the film follows three young adults drifting through work, friendship, and desire as summer gives way to an uncertain future. With its naturalistic performances, loose rhythms, and extraordinary sensitivity to time, place, and everyday gestures, Miyake finds profound emotional resonance in the ordinary, affirming his distinctive voice in contemporary Japanese cinema.” —Shun Inoue, Japan Foundation

And Your Bird Can Sing screens with August 8th, a short companion piece of sorts to And Your Bird Can Sing starring Shizuka Ishibashi.

August 8th (Sho Miyake, 2016, 13 mins)

And Your Bird Can Sing (Sho Miyake, 2018, 106 mins)

movies.title: Andrew Norman Wilson: Sound Works
movies.description:
Andrew Norman Wilson presents a selection of his disparate short works united by their shared attention to the aural, each beginning with or inspired by a sound, a song, or the spoken word. In a format inspired by VH1 Storytellers (1996-2015), the screening will be punctuated by Wilson discussing the manner in which sound shapes the creation and perception of his work. The evening’s bill of fare includes video art, music videos, narrative shorts, and the New York premiere of Silvesterchlausen (2025), exploring a little-known New Year’s Eve tradition whose origins remain wreathed in mystery, still practiced today in Switzerland’s most conservative region, the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

Filmmaker Andrew Norman Wilson in person for a special presentation on Saturday, December 12th

movies.title: Arco
movies.cast: Margot Ringard Oldra, Oscar Tresanini, Nathanaël Perrot, Alma Jodorowsky, Swann Arlaud, Vincent Macaigne
movies.description: In the year 2075, a 10-year-old girl witnesses a mysterious boy in a rainbow suit fall from the sky. Arco comes from an idyllic far future where time travel is possible. Iris shelters him, and will do whatever it takes to help him return to his time. In return, Arco gives Iris hope for an optimistic future. Directed by author and comic-book illustrator Ugo Bienvenu, this vivacious animated feature debuted at Cannes and won recognition from the New York Film Critics Online and Lumière Awards alongside dozens of prestigious nominations. Academy Award nominee, Best Animated Feature

movies.title: Art Cinema for Tots: Tales from the Forest
movies.description:
Born out of a commitment to the idea that it’s never too early to introduce kids to the pleasures of movies made outside of the commercial mainstream—and the suspicion that young audiences are often more open-minded and curious than their elders when it comes to such matters—Metrograph presents the latest iteration of Art Cinema for Tots, a celebration of handcrafted, kid-friendly films that reconcile the smart and the silly. In this edition, join us for Tales from the Forest, a quartet of films by venerable Russian animator Yuri Norstein, whose meticulous, slow-moving perfectionism—each minute of finished film is the result of untold hours of labor—long ago earned him the nickname “the Golden Snail.”

Director of Programming (and mom) Inge de Leeuw describes the experience: “The sound levels will be dimmed, and there will be a gentle light on, creating a relaxed atmosphere where young viewers feel at ease. They won’t be confined to their seats; they can move around, explore, and enjoy the wonder of the big screen. It will be a playful, interactive cinematic journey, designed with little explorers in mind.

Fox and the Hare (Yuri Norstein, 1973, 12 mins)

Heron and the Crane (Yuri Norstein, 1974, 10 mins)

Seasons (Yuri Norstein, 1969, 9 mins)

Hedgehog and the Fog (Yuri Norstein, 1975, 11 mins)

Each ticket includes free admission for one child, if you’d like to bring more than one child per ticket, please email [email protected] to book a seat.

movies.title: Backrooms
movies.cast: Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Finn Bennett, Lukita Maxwell, Mark Duplass, Avan Jogia
movies.description: Drawing on the deep dread of so-called “liminal” spaces—the non-places of depopulated office buildings and parking lots of late capitalist America—this feature debut from 20-year-old Kane Parsons was inspired by a sprawling fictional location first chronicled in a 2019 4chan thread. A simple premise straight out of the internet age snowballs into psychological terror as store-owner Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his therapist (Renate Reinsve) venture into an unknown dimension through a strange doorway that has appeared in the basement of a furniture showroom.

movies.title: Batman Returns
movies.cast: Michael Keaton, Danny DeVito, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken, Michael Gough, Pat Hingle
movies.description: Burton and star Michael Keaton’s first Caped Crusader film was a pop culture phenomenon; their second was no slouch at the box office itself, but an altogether spicier dish to serve to unsuspecting multiplex audiences: an unremittingly grim, gloomily gothic blockbuster featuring Danny DeVito as a grotesque Penguin, commanding a fleet of heavily armed flightless seabirds to raze Gotham City; a deliciously plummy Christopher Walken playing a corrupt industrialist who happens to share his name with the lead of F.W. Murnau’s Nosferatu ; and an ideal foil/love interest for Batman/Bruce Wayne in the form of Michelle Pfeiffer’s slinkily SM-suited Catwoman, putting her stamp on the role for time immemorial.
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Batman Returns
movies.cast: Michael Keaton, Danny DeVito, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken, Michael Gough, Pat Hingle
movies.description: Gotham City faces two monstrous criminal menaces: the bizarre, sinister Penguin (Danny DeVito) and the slinky, mysterious Catwoman (Michelle Pfeiffer). Can Batman (Michael Keaton) battle two formidable foes at once, especially when one wants to be mayor and the other is romantically attracted to Bruce Wayne? Like the groundbreaking 1989 original, BATMAN RETURNS is directed by the wizardly Tim Burton. And like the first blockbuster, it’s a dazzling adventure that leaves you breathless.

movies.title: Beauty and the Beast
movies.cast: Paige O'Hara, Robby Benson, Richard White, Jerry Orbach, David Ogden Stiers, Angela Lansbury
movies.description: Tale as old as time, song as old as rhyme… After lean years through the 1980s, Disney animation had a blockbuster breakthrough with 1989’s The Little Mermaid, and their follow-up, Beauty and the Beast, likewise featuring irresistible songs by the team of Howard Ashman and Alan Menken, proved that Mermaid was no one-off fluke—the House of the Mouse was back! Based on the fairy tale published in 1740 by Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve, Disney’s charming retelling introduces us to bright, bookish Belle; her boorish, preening suitor, Gaston; the leonine Beast, living in seclusion from prying eyes; a host of delightful animate household objects; and not less than three Best Original Song Oscar noms. Be our guest!
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Ben'imana
movies.cast: Clémentine U. Nyirinkindi, Kesia Kelly Nishimwe, Arivere Kagoyire, Isabelle Kabano, Antoinette Uwamahoro, Leocadie Uwabeza
movies.description:
In 2012, eighteen years after the genocide against the Tutsi, a Rwandan village is still learning how to live with itself. Vénéranda has spent years helping survivors and the families of those responsible speak the words that were never said between them. However, forgiveness comes easier when it’s someone else’s story. When her own daughter’s future becomes entangled with the past, Vénéranda is forced to find her own words at last.

Spanning three generations of women, BEN’IMANA is an intimate portrait of inherited silence — and the fragile question of whether people who have survived the unspeakable together can still build a life side by side.

movies.title: Best Pancakes in the County
movies.cast: Nicolas Cage, Justin Long, Shelley Hennig
movies.description: Set over the course of one explosive night, BEST PANCAKES IN THE COUNTY transforms an unassuming small-town diner into the epicenter of a deadly standoff involving rogue federal agents, a fast-talking con man with a dangerous past and a waitress harboring secrets of her own. As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.

movies.title: Bitter Christmas
movies.cast: Bárbara Lennie, Leonardo Sbaraglia, Aitana Sánchez-Gijón, Victoria Luengo, Patrick Criado, Milena Smit
movies.description: BITTER CHRISTMAS tells two alternating stories, one starring Elsa, an advertising director, in 2004, during a long weekend in December. The second takes place in 2026 and stars Raúl, a screenwriter and director who is writing a script that we soon discover is the story of Elsa, her boyfriend Bonifacio, and her friends Patricia and Natalia. Mixed with fiction, Elsa is, in a way, Raúl's alter ego, who, like him, resorts to autofiction as a solution to a long period of creative drought. He looks inside himself, and he can't help but also look at the people who make up his most intimate universe: his partner and his assistant. The film narrates the close relationship between reality and fiction, between inspiration and life, exploring the limits of autofiction and stories within stories.

movies.title: Blue + Chinese Series
movies.cast: Len Cariou, Joe Carter
movies.description: Over the same, unceasing monochromatic sea of blue, Yves Klein’s patented “International Klein Blue,” the voices of Jarman and collaborating actors (including Tilda Swinton and Nigel Terry) read a poetic text by the director in which he muses on the physical and mental deterioration wrought by the ravages of AIDS, as well as the endless implications of the color blue. Jarman would be gone within a year, but he left behind one of the great final films, a vibrant work of courage and clarity in the face of oblivion. Screens with Brakhage’s Chinese Series, a long-contemplated short work inspired by Chinese ideograms completed in the filmmaker’s dying days.

movies.title: Blue Heron
movies.cast: Eylul Guven, Iringó Réti, Ádám Tompa, Edik Beddoes, Amy Zimmer, Liam Serg
movies.description: In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by increasingly dangerous behavior from the eldest son, Jeremy. At wit’s end, their parents are presented with a shattering choice. Award-winning director Sophy Romvari’s semi-autobiographical debut feature is a lyrical, profound testament to the things we carry with us, masterfully chronicling the haze of a languid summer and the clarity of the moments that defined it. Q&A with director Sophy Romvari following the 4/21, 7pm screening

movies.title: Calamity
movies.cast: Bolek Polívka, Dagmar Bláhová, Jana Synková, Marie Pavlíková, Klára Emingerová, Jaroslava Kretschmerová
movies.description: Earning the disapproval and incomprehension of father and friends alike, Honza (Bolek Polívka, a physical comedian of rare gifts who would become a Chytilová regular) leaves his university studies for a job as a train engineer in a podunk mountain town, confronting the institutional rot of the state-controlled rail system as well as the machinations of three women (Dagmar Bláhová, Jaroslava Kretschmerová, and Jana Synková) who each have their romantic designs on our slacker antihero. A sex comedy with a satirical stiletto hidden up its sleeve, its climax—involving the train’s entrapment by an avalanche and ensuing anarchy—a masterpiece of comic chaos.

movies.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
movies.cast: Cameron Winter
movies.description: Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie. Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson ( One Battle After Another ), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie ( The Smashing Machine ) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele). GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a "a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork , Rolling Stone , Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker , NME , and Stereogum .

movies.title: Chronicle of Anna Magdalena Bach
movies.cast: Gustav Leonhardt, Christiane Lang, Paolo Carlini, Ernst Castelli, Hans-Peter Boye, Joachim Wolff
movies.description: Renowned harpsichordist Gustave Leonhardt plays—and plays as—Johann Sebastian Bach in Straub and Huillet’s remarkable film on the composer, based in part on a fictional journal by his second wife, and built around live-sound recordings of Leonhardt…

movies.title: Chronovisor
movies.cast: Anne Laure Sellier, Nicholas Tebben, Nicole Dombrowski Risser, Alex Kolodkin, José Pacheco de Almeida, Sophie Queuniet
movies.description: Béatrice (Anne Laure Sellier), a Columbia professor deep into research for a monograph on theories of memory throughout the ages, stumbles across the purportedly true story of the “Chronovisor,” a device said to be able to reproduce images from any point in history onto a television screen, and in short order her curiosity becomes an all-consuming monomania. (The genesis of Walker and Auen’s story is a claim by one Father Pellegrino Ernetti to have collaborated on the creation of just such an invention.) An ingenious archival conspiracy thriller that might have tickled Umberto Eco and Jorge Luis Borges, unfolding amidst the shadowy stacks of New York City’s libraries. “Wonderfully unclassifiable. A tantalizing armchair mystery steeped in occult-ish authenticity [and] a sly commentary on our own relationship to the pursuit of curiosity.”—Los Angeles Times
notes: Q&A with filmmakers Jack Auen and Kevin Walker moderated by Ryan Krivoshey, founder of Grasshopper Films, on Friday, December 11th

movies.title: Chronovisor
movies.cast: Anne Laure Sellier, Nicholas Tebben, Nicole Dombrowski Risser, Alex Kolodkin, José Pacheco de Almeida, Sophie Queuniet
movies.description: While writing a monograph on historical theories of memory, Béatrice, a respected academic, becomes beguiled by the allegedly true story of the Chronovisor, an occult device said to reproduce visuals from any point in history on a TV screen. Her obsession with the mysterious machine drags her from her Upper East Side apartment through the depths of New York City’s hidden libraries, to the edge of a breakthrough.

movies.title: Citizen Kane
movies.cast: Orson Welles, Dorothy Comingore, Joseph Cotten, Everett Sloane, George Coulouris, Agnes Moorehead
movies.description: Starting many of Orson Welles’ Mercury Players on the road to thriving film careers, Welles’ masterwork chronicles the stormy life of an influential publishing tycoon, rooted in themes of power, corruption, vanity — the American Dream lost in the mystery of a dying man’s last word: “Rosebud.”

movies.title: Club Kid

movies.description: A hard-partying New York City club promoter sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

This comedy-drama mixes the untamed world of nightlight with an unconventional story of fatherhood. Stranger things have happened in New York’s club scene.

movies.title: Columbus
movies.cast: John Cho, Haley Lu Richardson, Michelle Forbes, Rory Culkin, Parker Posey, Erin Allegretti
movies.description: Modern architecture acts as a vehicle for emotional expression in Kogonada’s lauded first feature, whose title refers to the Indiana city that, thanks to the patronage of Cummins diesel engines company cofounder J. Irwin Miller, has commissioned buildings from master builders including I.M. Pei, Eero Saarinen, and Robert Venturi. A Korean American translator (John Cho) arrives in this curious testing ground for advanced architecture after his estranged scholar father falls ill, there to cross paths with dad’s protégée (Parker Posey), an aesthete clerk at the local library (Haley Lu Richardson), and a bevy of singular structures. A film of rich colors and muted yearning, and one of the most distinctive debuts in the last decade of American independent cinema.
notes: Q&A with filmmaker Kogonada and actor Haley Lu Richardson moderated by filmmaker Christopher Radcliff on Sunday, November 8th

movies.title: Compartment No. 6
movies.cast: Seidi Haarla, Yura Borisov, Dinara Drukarova, Yuliya Aug, Lidiya Kostina, Tomi Alatalo
movies.description:
When her girlfriend bails on a planned trip to visit ancient petroglyphs in the remote city of Murmansk in the Arctic Circle, Finnish student Laura (Seidi Haarla) decides to go on alone, finding herself sharing a compartment on the long train from Moscow with Lyokha (Yura Borisov), a Russian returning to his work in the mines of the northeast who makes a belligerent and boorish first impression, but in time becomes a figure of fascination for Laura—and she for him.

“There are not enough films about uncategorizable love. Here is a marvelous corrective to that neglected genre.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue"

movies.title: Countercurrents
movies.description: Traumatized by his recent divorce, lovelorn Stanley takes off cross country to San Francisco, landing at his enterprising sister Nancy's doorstep. Nancy, who makes counterculture cinema-themed t-shirts, lives in "Camille's Castle," a frozen-in-time legacy home for displaced artists and outcasts. Together, they search for the remaining scraps of San Francisco's Summer of Love, and wind up at odds with each other. Countercurrents is an aggressive tribute to the counterculture films of the late 60's, with "easter eggs" in no short supply.

When the down-and-out attorney and Coyote realize they’ll be squaring off against the former’s ex-boss (Cena) in the case, it lights a fire under the duo—launching an unlikely friendship. The equally endearing and gut-busting adventure finally arrives in theaters after being shelved in 2023, giving Looney Tunes fans an opportunity to experience the whimsy of some of cinema’s most iconic cartoon stars back on the silver screen.

movies.title: Day Night Day Night
movies.cast: Luisa Williams, Josh Philip Weinstein, Gareth Saxe, Nyambi Nyambi, Frank Dattolo, Annemarie Lawless
movies.description: Before her epic My Undesirable Friends made Loktev one of the most-discussed figures in contemporary nonfiction, there was Day Night Day Night, the director’s riveting fiction feature debut, closely following 48 hours in the life of an unnamed young woman, played by an entrancing Luisa Colón, as she makes preparations to detonate herself in a Times Square suicide bombing in service to an unknown cause. Shot with remarkable immediacy and adroitness by cinematographer Benoît Debie, best known for his collaborations with Gaspar Noé, and lent a sense of subtly rising tension that reaches a point of near-suffocation by editor Michael Taylor, Loktev’s austere film—and its brooding, taciturn leading lady—exert a sinister undertow pull of fascination.

Idealistic Sheldon Mopes (Edward Norton) has always wanted to bring his character, Smoochy the Rhino, to children’s television, and when the top star at the Kid’s Net channel, “Rainbow” Randolph (Robin Williams), is arrested in a bribery scandal, he sees his chance… But as it transpires, hell hath no fury like a “Rainbow” Randolph scorned, and Sheldon’s sunny disposition will be sorely tested by his predecessor’s sabotage and the sleazy reality of the children’s entertainment biz. An acrid dark comedy, with DP Anastos Michos lending the whole affair an air of blighted cheeriness.

“I picked Death to Smoochy because it is about innocence for sale. In 2002, the press and the audience found its cynicism over the top. Now it is a cult classic and its narrative reads like reportage.” —Anastas Michos, ASC

When Rockwell unleashes a globe-threatening disaster, he embarks on a frantic mission to prove to humanity—his sister, (Hüller), the president (Goodman), the VP (Stuhlbarg), a scientist (Ahmed), and, well, everyone—that he is humanity’s savior. Spielberg’s latest sci-fi movie event, his first film since 2022’s The Fabelmans , returns to a legacy of grand, other-worldly, mysterious spectacle. Starring Emily Blunt ( Oppenheimer ), Josh O’Connor ( Challengers ), and Colin Firth ( The King’s Speech ), Disclosure Day thrills in the tense moment when the unknown becomes known.

movies.title: Dov’è la Libertà?
movies.cast: Totò, Vera Molnar, Nyta Dover
movies.description: Incarcerated for twenty-two years after committing a crime of passion, Salvatore Lojacono (Totò) wins parole and returns to a Rome that he scarcely recognizes—and ultimately decides that prison is preferable. Salvatore learns the hard way that business, romance, and family are all elaborate rackets; even the most sympathetic victim he encounters is just on the hunt for a tax swap. His disenchantment is recounted in flashback, as he begs a judge to lock him back up. (The courtroom scenes were, in fact, shot later by Mario Monicelli, after Rossellini abandoned the project in mid-production, and effectively bridged the patchwork of episodes left behind.) The popular Neapolitan comedian Totò gets plenty of opportunities to mug, but also flexes his dramatic muscles as a man who trusts too tenderly. The scenario was inspired by Chaplin’s MODERN TIMES, but the moral vision is closer to MONSIEUR VERDOUX, another comedy born of the recognition that post-war society has been stripped of sentimental illusions and re-organized under principles of ruthless capitalism indistinguishable from the barbarism it displaced. “It stupefied me with its cruelty and bitterness,” wrote Pierre Kast in Cahiers du Cinema , long a bastion of Rossellini apologetics. “It’s a parable of the purest Swiftian type, unpitying and almost intolerable.”

movies.title: Drama! Experiments! Brilliant Finale!
movies.description:
“Drama! Experiments! Brilliant Finale! begins with a documentary film showing a central scene of early cinema: the fairground. A drama in the same milieu follows, the first film in our series by Albert Capellani, who, in 1906, began to transform early cinema by introducing the art of mise en scène. (His innovative, practically avant-garde The Bell Ringer’s Daughter ends the program along with Gaston Velle's Tit-for-Tat.") Next, four films that reveal the experimental side of early cinema: experimentation with color systems in the Kinematograph test reels of Tartans of Scottish Clans, the genesis of animation in Humorous Phases of Funny Faces, a kind of proto-surrealism in And the Villain Still Pursued Her, and a mixture of different experimental techniques, including scratching the film surface, in Gaston Velle’s Victims of the Storm. It is important to note that experimentation took place everywhere—in France, the US, and the UK. With the invention of so many techniques, the early cinema period was the most experimental in film history, it’s a shame that it is so often excluded from the history of experimental cinema. Trip Down Niagara Falls is a representative scène de plein air, a 'genre’ that brings the wide world to audiences—here in gorgeous color. The final film, the above-mentioned Tit-for-Tat, is a vibrant scène à trucs (trick film) full of magnificent techniques, and one of the earliest films in history promoting environmental awareness, conveying its message in an incredibly charming way.” —Series curator Karl Wratschko

While the last couple of decades have been pretty sparse when it comes to quality Christmas movies, ELF, the 2003 Will Ferrell comedy, undoubtedly has taken a corner seat at this proverbial table of fame.

movies.title: Empathy and Disaster
movies.description:
“The films of Empathy and Disaster depict events in the real world—or a staged re-enactment of them. Both create an immediate experience of reality, and stir feelings of empathy, regardless of how the images on the screen, ‘real’ or ‘fictional,’ were created. Today’s viewers should consider that one of the characteristics of early cinema is that it had not yet been standardized and sanitized, and therefore images that might, according to contemporary norms, be considered too crude were often uncensored. This program illuminates the fact that evoking empathy in an audience is one of the foremost aims of cinema, and had indeed already been perfected by 1906. It also shows that the boundary between nonfiction and fiction was already very porous in early cinema, and that much of what we now regard as a ‘hybrid’ film form has its origins in early cinema (e.g. The Alps by Telescope).” —Series curator Karl Wratschko

Featuring gorgeous location photography, suicidal stuntwork on speeding period locomotives, and bone-breaking action, Emperor of the North is Aldrich at his brutal best.

“Where a tramp is headed matters less than how long he can stay on the train, at least where it concerns the #19, ruled by the sadistic, bulging-eyed Shack. Outmaneuvering him becomes an irresistible challenge for seasoned hobos and, for railway workers who despise him just as much, a betting sport.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: Europa '51
movies.cast: Ingrid Bergman, Alexander Knox, Giulietta Masina, Ettore Gianini
movies.description: Shortly after completing THE FLOWERS OF ST. FRANCIS, Rossellini seized upon a hypothetical: if Francis himself appeared in Europe today and preached his humble doctrine, he would be promptly thrown in an insane asylum. Augmented by ideas derived from Simone Weil and Herbert Marcuse, Rossellini’s thought experiment grew and grew until it became EUROPA ’51, a sweeping state-of-the-continent address aimed at the complacency of post-war society. Luckily, Rossellini retained the services of his wife to put a box office spin on this dense rumination. (It would become, ironically, the only one of their pictures together to do any business in Italy.) Irene Gerard (Ingrid Bergman) is a socialite who’s more focused on throwing a good dinner party than attending to the needs of her young son. When the boy kills himself, Irene’s world is shattered: what could drive a child to so thoroughly reject life, and what can she make of the life that remains? Inspired by her cousin’s commitment to the class struggle, Irene begins devoting her time to Rome’s downtrodden. After all, the sick, the dying, and the poor need her more than her husband (Alexander Knox) ever could, do they not? Is Bergman preaching Communist revolution, Christian neighborliness, or some obscure, hyper-personal fusion of the two? Disarmingly literal and unspeakably sincere in its spiritual crusade, EUROPA ‘51 remains the most mysterious of Bergman and Rossellini’s collaborations.

movies.title: Fatherland
movies.cast: Hanns Zischler, Sandra Hüller
movies.description: From the director of IDA and COLD WAR: FATHERLAND follows Nobel Prize-winning author Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler, KINGS OF THE ROAD) and his actress daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller, ANATOMY OF A FALL) as they drive across a war-ravaged 1949 Germany. Returning home after years of exile in the U.S. and exuding a superhuman gravitas, Mann finds the Germany he knew to be gone, replaced by a country with contradictory ideologies. Erika, who acts as his travel coordinator and translator, strives to pierce his detached persona while quietly struggling with a family tragedy.

movies.title: Female Trouble
movies.cast: Divine, Mink Stole, David Lochary, Edith Massey, Mary Vivian Pearce, Cookie Mueller
movies.description:
“Sex offenses that would shock the Marquis de Sade!” sniffed critic Rex Reed in the Daily News, reviewing John Waters’ follow-up to the notorious Pink Flamingos . The perversities pile up in the tale of high-school delinquent and meatball sandwich-lover Dawn Davenport (played by Waters muse Divine), whose number one Christmas wish is for a pair of cha-cha heels. But her parents fail to heed her request, and her rage leads inexorably to stripping, prostitution, disfigurement, tabloid fame and mass murder.

Shot in Waters’ beloved native Baltimore on 16mm and featuring his regular Dreamlanders troupe–including Mink Stole, David Lochary, Mary Vivian Pearce, Edith Massey, and Cookie Mueller–this endlessly quotable, gloriously lurid satire was Divine’s favorite of his own films.

“The sordid tale of Dawn Davenport, who rises from high school hoyden to mistress of crime… A true original.” – Variety

The MEET THE PARENTS series gave us one of comedy's all-time great exchanges: "I've got nipples, Greg. Can you milk me?" Now Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro are back, with Skyler Gisondo (having quite a year on the big screen) playing Stiller's son, Henry, who's ready to pop the question to his girlfriend Olivia (Ariana Grande), a former FBI hostage negotiator. The lie detector is back, Jack Byrnes is looking pretty jacked, and the concept “baby birding” is introduced.

Fun fact: the original MEET THE PARENTS was based on a 1992 short film produced by comedian Emo Phillips. Drop that knowledge to your moviegoing pal and wait for the accolades to pour in.

movies.title: Forbidden Planet
movies.cast: Walter Pidgeon, Anne Francis, Leslie Nielsen, Warren Stevens, Jack Kelly, Earl Holliman
movies.description: Take the bones of William Shakespeare’s The Tempest, move the action to the far-flung planet “Altair IV,” and gussy up the proceedings in CinemaScope and Eastmancolor and you’ve got this triumph of high ’50s science fiction. Commander Adams (Leslie Nielsen) touches down on the remote planet to find the only signs of life remaining from an earlier expedition are Dr. Morbius (Walter Pidgeon), daughter Altaira (Anne Francis), and their mechanical servant. The iconic Robby the Robot would be an influence on much sci-fi to come, but no less impactful was the pioneering electronic soundtrack by Bebe and Louis Baron, the first fully electronic score for a major motion picture.

movies.title: From Russia with Love
movies.cast: Sean Connery, Daniela Bianchi, Pedro Armendáriz, Robert Shaw, Lotte Lenya, Bernard Lee
movies.description:
Connery’s briskly paced, whip-smart second outing as MI6 agent James Bond has 007 assigned to aid in the defection of Russian spy Tatiana Romanova (Daniela Bianchi) in Istanbul, where he’ll face hard resistance from the international criminal organization SPECTRE. From here the two will have to fight their way across the former Yugoslavia towards a final showdown in Venice, reckoning along the way with SPECTRE agents like Lotte Lenya’s Klebb and Robert Shaw’s “Red” Grant, acting under the command of Anthony Dawson’s mysterious Blofeld. One of the best-loved of all Bonds, and the film with which producer Albert Broccoli believed “the Bond style and formula were perfected.”

“Don’t trust the people you meet on trains! Even James Bond, who rarely makes mistakes, lets his judgment momentarily slide when he’s traveling aboard the sumptuous Orient Express. Featuring Robert Shaw’s second (and barely recognizable) appearance in this series.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

movies.title: General Della Rovere
movies.cast: Vittorio De Sica, Hannes Messemer, Sandra Milo, Anne Vernon
movies.description: Based on the true story of Italian cavalry officer Giovanni Bertone during World War II, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE recounts the unexpected moral evolution of Emanuele Bardone (Vittorio de Sica), an ingratiating swindler with a talent for improvising novel solutions to the dilemmas he has sprung on himself. Alas, even when Bardone wins, he feels compelled to double-down and gamble away his momentary advantage. He has a talent for extracting favors from the Nazi officers in Genoa, and when the law catches up to Bardone, he’s offered a bargain: go to prison and imitate the Italian general Della Rovere, in hopes of penetrating his resistance network. De Sica’s big and boisterous performance anchors the film, and renders this somber story of ethical compromise into an improbable crowdpleaser. Rossellini considered GENERAL DELLA ROVERE an embarrassing capitulation, a work-for-hire to demonstrate that he could, under duress, follow a script and a schedule. Shot quickly on studio sets with some undisguised rear projection footage, GENERAL DELLA ROVERE went on to win the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival and revitalize Rossellini’s career after a decade of box office setbacks. Like Bardone, Rossellini always had another trick up his sleeve.

movies.title: Germany, Year Zero
movies.cast: Edmund Moeschke, Ernst Pittschau, Ingetraud Hinze
movies.description: Following the international acclaim and box office success of ROME, OPEN CITY and PAISAN, Rossellini took the first of many obstreperous swerves that would come to define his career. His next film would be another dispatch from war-torn Europe, with scenes playing out amidst the rubble with unvarnished immediacy, with unfamiliar and nonprofessional actors populating the cast—but this time, the protagonists would not be resistance fighters liberating Italy, but the defeated Germans muddling through their wasteland reich. Financed largely by the French government, GERMANY, YEAR ZERO became an experiment in radical empathy and its limits, casting about for signs of new life in a nation of crooks, unrepentant Nazis, and pederasts. The only innocent soul is twelve-year-old protagonist Edmund, who cannot qualify for a work permit, but must somehow earn a living to support his household. Even the child recognizes that he has no role models in this world: his brother is a mopey ex-soldier who refuses to register for a ration card, his father is an invalid who muses he’d be better off dead, his neighbors are coarse and severe, his friends are common swindlers, and his former school teacher still preaches that the strong must snuff out the weak. Unsentimental in the extreme and devoid of any comic relief, GERMANY YEAR ZERO plays like a seance for souls who have yet to recognize themselves as the walking dead.

movies.title: Gertrud
movies.cast: Nina Pens Rode, Bendt Rothe, Ebbe Rode, Baard Owe, Axel Strøbye, Karl Gustav Ahlefeldt
movies.description: Based on a 1906 play of the same name by Swedish novelist and playwright Hjalmar Söderberg, Dreyer’s curtain call stars Nina Pens Rode as Gertrud Kanning, an unhappily married retired opera singer who’s pulled hither and thither by various suitors, steadfast in her faith in the power of love through many an emotional buffeting. Dreyer, whose dedication to patient long takes and shunning of cinematic artifice here proved divisive on the film’s release, would respond to his critics: “What I seek in my films… is a penetration to my actors’ profound thoughts by means of their most subtle expressions… not the technique of cinema. Gertrud is a film that I made with my heart.”
notes: Presented in 35mm

movies.title: Godzilla
movies.cast: Akira Takarada, Momoko Kôchi, Akihiko Hirata, Takashi Shimura, Fuyuki Murakami, Sachio Sakai
movies.description: The O.G. kaiju, a walking volcano of a beast who can flatten a Tokyo neighborhood with a single sweep of his tail, makes his screen debut in this appetite-for-destruction smash-up from master of monsters Honda, a strikingly somber first entry in the franchise which links the awakening of the ancient Gojira to the imbalance of nature represented by the dawning of the Atomic Age. Catch this pop culture landmark the way it was meant to be seen in the original Japanese version, with all the destruction and none of the pontificating Raymond Burr.

movies.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
movies.cast: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Min Tanaka, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Masami Nagasawa, Yuki Yamada
movies.description: War reduced Japan to zero. Godzilla plunged it into minus. Now the math gets even more terrifying. Takashi Yamazaki returns to direct, write, and oversee the visual effects for this epic follow-up to GODZILLA MINUS ONE, his Oscar-winning reinvention of Toho’s iconic monster. Set in 1949, two years after the events of the previous film, GODZILLA MINUS ZERO follows Japan’s hard-fought recovery as a new catastrophe threatens to erase it all. With returning stars Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, bigger monster mayhem, and spectacular effects built for a huge screen, this is the latest chapter in a storied franchise that began in 1954. See the King of the Monsters at its most colossal, on the big screen.
notes: Presented in Japanese with English subtitles

movies.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
movies.cast: Lee Kang-sheng, Chen Shiang-Chyi, Kiyonobu Mitamura, Miao Tian, Shih Chun, Chen Chao-jung
movies.description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King Hu’s 1967 wuxia epic Dragon Inn, playing to a motley smattering of spectators, including two stars of Hu’s original opus, Miao Tien and Shih Chun, watching their younger selves with tears in their eyes.

movies.title: Greetings from Out Here
movies.description: Accompanied by her dog Sam and a video camera, filmmaker Ellen Spiro traveled from Virginia to Texas and back exploring openly gay culture in the Deep South. Highlighted by spontaneous encounters with local eccentrics and mechanics (her van breaks down frequently), Greetings from Out Here provides detailed portraits of small-town queer Southerners—from Rita, a retired military officer turned drag queen in New Orleans to Iris, a Black lesbian living in a bus in the Ozarks. Filmed on location at the Texas Gay Rodeo, Mardi Gras, Gay Pride in Atlanta, Dollywood, Miss Miller's Eternal Love and Care Pet Cemetery, and the Short Mountain Radical Faerie sanctuary, Spiro captures the richness, vitality and courage of "out" gay Southern life in the early 1990s.

movies.title: Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty
movies.description: Haru and Luis love competing in Tokyo’s ballroom dance scene, but after tragedy strikes, Haru withdraws into isolation. When friends coax her back to the studio, she develops an infatuation with the new instructor and must face what comes next as sparks fly. Steeped in sorrow but bursting with joy, Wladyk’s tight feature marries exhilarating choreography with equally dynamic camera movement, cultivating a vibrant visual ode to dance and its power to transcend grief.

movies.title: Hail Mary preceded by The Book of Mary
movies.cast: Myriem Roussel, Thierry Rode, Philippe Lacoste, Manon Andersen, Malachi Jara Kohan, Juliette Binoche
movies.description:
Denounced by Pope John Paul II and hordes of protestors and full-throatedly endorsed by John Waters (“my favorite foreign film since The Moon in the Gutter… hysterically funny”), Godard’s Hail Mary offers a contemporary retelling of the virgin birth of Jesus, with the Mother of God (Myriem Roussel) as the chaste teen daughter of a Swiss gas station owner, fiancé Joseph a cab driver, and the angel Gabriel arriving via jet plane. (As ever, no one shoots commercial airlines more beautifully than Godard.) Screens with Anne-Marie Miéville’s The Book of Mary, a study of an 11-year-old girl who, as her parents announce their separation, withdraws into a private world of books, music, and dance.

The Book of Mary (Anne-Marie Miéville, 1985, 28 mins)

Hail Mary (Jean Luc Goddard, 1985, 80 mins)

movies.title: Hamnet
movies.cast: Jessie Buckley, Paul Mescal, Emily Watson, Joe Alwyn, Jacobi Jupe, Noah Jupe
movies.description: In 16th-century England, an impoverished Latin tutor named William Shakespeare (Mescal) meets free-spirited Agnes (Buckley), sparking an affair that leads to marriage and three children. As Will seeks his fortune in the London theater, Agnes anchors the domestic sphere alone. The couple’s bond is tested when tragedy strikes, but their shared experience sets the stage for the creation of Shakespeare’s timeless masterpiece, Hamlet . Academy Award-winning filmmaker Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland , The Rider ) illuminates the complexities of love and the healing power of art and creativity.

movies.title: Hexed
movies.director: Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, Josie Trinidad
movies.cast: Tracey Ullman, Hailee Steinfeld, Walton Goggins, Rashida Jones, Jodie Foster, Stephen Fry
movies.description: An impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice, they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

movies.title: Hexed
movies.director: Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, Josie Trinidad
movies.cast: Tracey Ullman, Hailee Steinfeld, Walton Goggins, Rashida Jones, Jodie Foster, Stephen Fry
movies.description: You know what suburbia needs? More witchcraft. When teenage misfit Billie Doe discovers she has magical powers, her perfectly ordinary life takes a hard left into Hexe, a sprawling witch realm full of family secrets, three-eyed cats, and sentient microwaves. Arrive early for our ad-free pre-show of witchy clips to get the incantations started before the movie.

movies.title: Hope
movies.cast: Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Hoyeon, Alicia Vikander, Michael Fassbender, Taylor Russell
movies.description: In the remote South Korean village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the area. In a forest nearby, a party of hunters including Sung-ki (Zo In-sung) set out to track the beast, only to find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading: what begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through into a tragedy of cosmic proportions. Premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, Hope “races from modern-day western to action thriller to horror film to science-fiction epic—all while retaining the full-throttle energy and sweaty cult-movie atmosphere of a 1970s exploitation flick,” according to the BBC.

movies.title: How to Rob a Bank
movies.cast: Nicholas Hoult, Zoë Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Rhenzy Feliz, Pete Davidson, John C. Reilly
movies.description: We love a good heist movie, especially when the getaway is as stylish as the score. In HOW TO ROB A BANK, JOHN WICK director David Leitch brings his kinetic action sensibilities to a crew of social media-savvy robbers (Nicholas Hoult, Pete Davidson) who broadcast their daring heists for the world to see. But viral fame attracts the wrong kind of attention, and a veteran FBI agent (John C. Reilly) and a brilliant software engineer (Zoë Kravitz) are closing in. Assemble your wolfpack and catch this one on the big screen.

movies.title: I Love Boosters
movies.cast: Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie, Taylour Paige, Poppy Liu, Eiza González, LaKeith Stanfield
movies.description: In another surreal, politically-charged, and straight-up weird outing from eccentric director Boots Riley ( Sorry to Bother You ), I Love Boosters follows a crew of professional shoplifters (Keke Palmer, Naomi Ackie) as they take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven (Demi Moore)—in an effort they deem a community service. Sneak preview screening on May 19 at 7:30pm followed by a Q&A with Boots Riley

movies.title: I Play Rocky
movies.cast: Anthony Ippolito, AnnaSophia Robb, P.J. Byrne, Toby Kebbell, Jay Duplass, Tracy Letts
movies.description: I PLAY ROCKY is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn't just meant to write Rocky – he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told "no" at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.

movies.title: I Want Your Sex
movies.cast: Olivia Wilde, Cooper Hoffman, Mason Gooding, Chase Sui Wonders, Johnny Knoxville, Margaret Cho
movies.description: The latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Gregg Araki ( Mysterious Skin , The Doom Generation , White Bird in a Blizzard ), I Want Your Sex follows Elliot, a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething (Hoffman), whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes young Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the lines between satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder blur through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

movies.title: Imitation of Life
movies.cast: Lana Turner, John Gavin, Sandra Dee, Susan Kohner, Robert Alda, Dan O'Herlihy
movies.description: Sirk’s supreme tearjerker, this stealth investigation into race in America takes the form of a deceptively glossy melodrama, with bottle-blonde Lana Turner as Lora, a single mother trying to raise a daughter and start an acting career. But as the film unfolds with Sirk’s usual visual splendor, he undercuts his own main narrative, focusing more intently on the fraught relationship between Lora’s African American maid, Annie, and her mixed-race daughter, Sarah Jane, played by Juanita Moore and Susan Kohner in Oscar-nominated roles. (An unexpected visit by Annie to Sarah Jane’s classroom at Christmas time is but one of many devastating moments.) Arguably the film’s most eloquent review comes from none other than Richard Pryor, in 1959 serving with the Army and stationed in West Germany, who was thrown in the brig after stabbing a white soldier who laughed through an on-base screening.

movies.title: In Bed with Victoria
movies.cast: Virginie Efira, Vincent Lacoste, Melvil Poupaud, Laurent Poitrenaux, Laure Calamy, Alice Daquet
movies.description: High-powered lawyer Victoria (Efira) is an unstoppable force in the courtroom, but off the clock she struggles to raise her two daughters on her own, respond to the latest online defamation from her vindictive ex-husband, and feign more than passing interest in her latest app-arranged fuck-and-run. While wrapped up in a singularly unusual case brought to her by an old pal (Melvil Poupaud), Victoria reconnects with a onetime client (Vincent Lacoste) who seems to offer the prospect of something more than a desultory fling… that is, if she’s ready or able to accept what’s on offer. A frisky, funny showcase for Efira, unforgettable as the pouty, rumpled, restless, reckless Victoria, smart and savvy in its upending of rom-com cliché.
notes: Introduction by actress Virginie Efira on Friday, November 13th

movies.title: India: Matri Bhumi
movies.description:
Fed up with narrative filmmaking and invited by prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru to make a film in India, Rossellini embarked upon an adventure in documentary filmmaking. At the conclusion of his odyssey, Rossellini would have a ten-episode television series, a feature film, an Indian government renouncing any and all support, and another intercontinental romantic scandal. (He would eventually marry his scenarist Sonali Senroy Das Gupta, with whom he would have two children.) INDIA: MATRI BHUMI is an encyclopedic effort to catalog the varied geographic, ethnic, religious, natural, and architectural dimensions of life in India, a majestic kaleidoscope that never stops turning. Upon its debut at Cannes in 1959, Jean-Luc Godard would proclaim that to watch INDIA: MATRI BHUMI was to witness “the creation of the world.”

Rossellini spent significant time in Chile in the early 1970s, chasing various projects that never got off the ground. He did manage, however, to befriend Salvador Allende, and conduct an interview with him in May 1971. Italian television station RAI acquired the interview, but did not air it until 1973, after Pinochet’s coup and Allende’s death sparked renewed interest in the conversation.

movies.title: Ink
movies.cast: Jack O’Connell, Claire Foy, Guy Pearce
movies.description: The film is an explosive cinematic rollercoaster about a group of visionaries and misfits who had an idea for a new kind of news — one that would give the people what they want and would change the face of the world we live in today.

movies.title: Is This Thing On?
movies.cast: Will Arnett, Laura Dern, Andra Day, Bradley Cooper, Christine Ebersole, Ciarán Hinds
movies.description: As their marriage quietly unravels, Alex (Arnett) faces middle age and an impending divorce, seeking new purpose in the New York comedy scene while Tess (Dern) confronts the sacrifices she made for their family—forcing them to navigate co-parenting, identity, and whether love can take a new form. Bradley Cooper writes, directs, and co-stars in this understated, affecting portrait of the challenges and opportunities of starting over in middle age.

movies.title: It Ends
movies.cast: Billy Bush, Michael DeBarge
movies.description: A group of recent grads head out on a late-night drive for grub, hoping to enjoy one final hangout before their paths diverge. Instead, they accidentally turn onto an endless two-lane hellscape surrounded by untold horrors and cosmic forces beyond their understanding. Written, directed, and edited by Alexander Ullom in his directorial debut, It Ends premiered at the 2025 South by Southwest Festival, and has been praised by Variety as a “brilliant” modern retelling of Jean-Paul Sartre’s No Exit .

movies.title: It Follows
movies.cast: Maika Monroe, Keir Gilchrist, Daniel Zovatto, Jake Weary, Olivia Luccardi, Lili Sepe
movies.description: Mitchell’s Detroit-shot sophomore film, winner of the Next Wave award at Austin’s Fantastic Fest in 2014 and the breakout horror phenomenon of the following year, is a work of potent sexual dread, in which erotic congress transmits something much worse than a dose of clap: the attentions of a spectral, shape-shifting entity that pursues the afflicted with methodical single-mindedness, a pursuit that ends in terrible carnage. Enigmatic and unsettling, its thick atmosphere of paranoia incalculably added to by a soundtrack courtesy electronic musician Disasterpiece (Rich Vreeland), per Pitchfork “a score that announces when something is about to happen, only to suddenly upend expectations and leave the room on edge.”

movies.title: Josephine
movies.cast: Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan, Phillip Ettinger
movies.description: JOSEPHINE follows the psychological fallout after eight-year-old Josephine (Mason Reeves) witnesses a brutal crime in Golden Gate Park. As she acts out, her parents (Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) struggle with helping their daughter cope, while facing the moral responsibility of demanding justice in a world that’s lost its innocence.
